intended_object: A specific witness assignment used inside a proof. Row i of a k×k anchored family gets the set of left-side anchor points {inl n : n in low k}, or {inl n : n in high k}, depending on whether i lies in the first half of the indices. The source is the docstring and the surrounding file, "Witness assignments attaining the anchored lower bounds".
explanation: The definition is an auxiliary construction. Together with colWitness, it builds the explicit witness assignment (upperAssignment) that shows the anchored lower bound on finite-witness width is attained. The body picks the left anchors indexed by the first half of the indices (rounded up) when i is in that half, and those indexed by the second half otherwise. The private lemmas row_card and row_anchor then use exactly the cardinality and membership properties this choice gives. It is a choice made for one proof, not a standard notion from the literature, so there is nothing to compare it with or to generalize.
